items.title: Union Health Ministry Proposes Immediate Suspension of Manufacturing Licences for Drugs Found Not of Standard Quality on Specified Critical Parameters
items.summary: The proposed amendments seek to enable prompt regulatory intervention upon detection of substandard medicines, prevent their continued manufacture and distribution, and strengthen the mechanism for ensuring compliance with prescribed quality standards, in the interest of patient safety and public health.

facts.text: The proposed arrangement is aimed at ensuring timely communication of NSQ findings to the relevant authorities and stakeholders, thereby facilitating coordinated regulatory action and strengthening accountability across the drug manufacturing and marketing chain.

The proposed amendments follow deliberations at the 65th meeting of the Drugs Consultative Committee (DCC), held on 20 December 2024, and recommendations of the 92nd meeting of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), held on 24 April 2025.

The amendments are expected to strengthen post-marketing regulatory surveillance, facilitate timely action against substandard medicines, promote greater accountability among manufacturers and marketers, and reinforce public confidence in the quality of medicines available in the country.

items.title: A Rulebook Alone Cannot Guarantee Dignity; Every Hand in Aviation Must Ensure It: Manmeet Kaur Nanda
items.summary: Highlighting the human cost of inaccessible air travel, Ms. Nanda recounted the experience of a para-athlete who had to travel to Egypt and compete in an international sporting event using a broken wheelchair after her original wheelchair was damaged by an airline. Despite this ordeal, the athlete went on to win a medal.

facts.text: Describing such experiences as barriers that the entire aviation ecosystem must collectively eliminate, she stressed that airlines, airport operators, ground-handling personnel, security agencies, customs and immigration officials must undergo regular induction and refresher training.

Calling for measurable accountability, she advocated accessibility performance indicators, time-bound grievance redressal mechanisms and dedicated dashboards to monitor the performance of airlines and airports.
